name: P22 Protocol B: the concise check record with a coding agent
status_note: Machine form of the proposal. Nothing is registered. The owner approves the measured run and registers it with a commit and a tag. A harness change after the pilot needs a new pilot. Pilot data stay out of the measured analysis.
question: In the experiment 5 agent setup, does the concise-1 C3 feedback keep the repairs, and does it change agent effort, compared with the current full-1 C3 feedback?

agent.cli_version_rule: Use 2.0.2 if it is still available. Record the actual CLI version and the logged model. Another CLI version needs a statement at registration.
agent.sandbox: the existing Seatbelt profile of agent_repair.py
agent.check_client: the existing opaque check client of agent_repair.py
agent.workspace: a fresh workspace for each session
agent.kimi_home: Do not edit the Kimi home configuration.

provider: The Kimi service behind the CLI. The CLI chooses the endpoint.

response_budget.per_request: The CLI default. The wire logs of experiments 4 and 5 record maxTokens 1,048,576.
response_budget.per_session: 100 steps and 900 seconds are the effective budget.

F.feedback: The unchanged experiment 5 C3 feedback: the build and run header, the line === evo diagnostics, the check record, one explain record per code and the plan record.
commands: the sealed assembly, link and run

K.feedback: The same header, the line === evo diagnostics, and one concise-1 check record. No explain or plan record.
commands: the sealed assembly, link and run
K.treatment_note: In this sandbox the agent cannot call evo explain, so K also removes the page examples. Report this as part of the treatment.

rules: The Rust lane has implemented concise-1 as p22-feedback-design.md describes, and its tests pass.

full-1 equals the EvoCC part of the 48 frozen C3 strings in tests/fixtures/agent-repair-4/qualification.json, after scratch-path replacement and the T03s completion-scope correction, and differs in no other byte. The raw byte-identical count is recorded as well.
The 48 concise-1 strings for the same sources are recorded before registration.

order.rule: Sorted items. Zero-based even indices run F first, odd indices K first. Repetition 2 reverses repetition 1.
order.harness: agent_repair.py run --order protocol-b --reps 2 runs repetition 1, then repetition 2.

predictions.B1: No repair loss. b counts item-repetition pairs repaired only with full-1; c counts pairs repaired only with concise-1. B1 holds when b - c is at most 2 of the 48 pairs. Report the exact two-sided McNemar p-value as a description.
predictions.B2: Tokens. concise-1 uses fewer total tokens, including cached input, per item mean. Exact one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test over 24 items, with zero differences dropped and midranks for ties, as in experiment 5.
predictions.B3: Steps. concise-1 uses fewer steps per item mean. Same test.
predictions.B4: Controls. On the six controls, the concise-1 step total is lower than the full-1 total. This is a point comparison without a test.
predictions.correction: Holm's correction over B2 and B3 at a family level of 0.05.
predictions.descriptive: EvoCC feedback bytes per check result, carried feedback tokens, check runs, wall time, audit counts and per-class tables.

power.accounting: The accounting predicts a token saving of about 1.8% if the agent's behavior does not change.
power.smallest_effect: With 24 items and two repetitions per arm, the smallest effect with 80% power at one-sided 0.05 is about 16% of steps or tokens.
power.basis: In experiment 5 part A, one C3 session varied within an item by a standard deviation of 1.73 steps and 32,690 tokens.
power.purpose: B2 and B3 can show only a large change in behavior. The main purpose is B1: a harm check before any change of default.

scoring.repair: The unchanged hidden driver under the three sealed builds. A repair needs a completed session and all three builds.
scoring.censored: A timeout or step limit counts as not repaired and keeps its effort.
scoring.unknown: A provider failure, scoring error or escape is unknown.

stopping.quota_reads: Read the quota before every session and at the end. A failed read stops the package.
stopping.week_ratio: Stop at the initial 7-day ratio plus 0.15, or at an absolute ratio of 0.85, whichever is lower.
stopping.five_hour: Wait out a 5-hour ratio at or above 0.90, by the existing pacing rule.
stopping.overload: Allow three CLI 429 overload notices per session. The fourth ends the session as provider_overloaded. Retry it once after all initial sessions.
stopping.refusal: A quota, limit or usage 429, or an authentication refusal, stops the package.
stopping.reruns: Rerun no other session. Use the final authorized retry, never the best one.
stopping.disk: Do not start below 25 GiB of free disk space. Stop below 15 GiB.

cost.basis: Experiment 5 part A C3 sessions: 5.54 requests and 102,564 tokens per session (98,096 cached input, 3,633 uncached input, 835 output). Part A raised the 7-day ratio by 0.085899 for 12,425,299 tokens: about 6.91e-9 per token. Planning bounds use the largest part A C3 session: 13 steps and 295,444 tokens. The hard cap is 100 requests per session.
cost.stop_line: The stop line limits the ratio increase to 0.15 in every case.

pilot.order_rule: Each item runs once in F and once in K, with F first for the first, third and fifth item. The protocol gives no table. The sessions follow the item order of the protocol text: agent_repair.py run --order pilot-b.
go_criteria: Every K check result with EvoCC output starts its EvoCC part with `{"form":"concise-1"`.
When the agent checks the unchanged `program.c`, the EvoCC part of the F result equals the frozen string for that source after path replacement and the T03s scope correction.
Every quota read succeeds. The harness records steps, tokens and scores.
pilot.note: Pilot data stay out of the analysis. The five items stay in the population.

measured.status: Not approved. The owner decides on the measured run after the pilot result.
measured.order: agent_repair.py run --order protocol-b --reps 2 --dry-run prints the 96-session order. Commit it before the first request.

harm_check_only.status: Not approved. A variant of the measured run.
harm_check_only.rule: Repetition 1 alone. B1 then holds when b - c is at most 1 of 24. Drop B2 and B3, because their power is too low.

reporting: Report F and K side by side for all 24 items and per class.
Report unknown, unattempted and censored counts separately.
State the limits: one model, one effort setting, shared kernels and injected defects.
Do not claim a causal effect of feedback length unless B2 or B3 holds. Even then, name the whole change: shorter records and no page examples.
harness_rules: The K record comes from evo check --json --form=concise-1 FILE, the argument order of the recorded fixture. An empty standard output gives standard error, as for each c3 record.
The c3 and k header come from one function, so K has the F header by construction.
The check log names the request id and the SHA-256 of the checked file. The go evaluation uses them to find checks of an unchanged corpus source. The served bytes do not change.
protocol-b and pilot-b fix the conditions c3 and k, the model, effort, wall limit, step limit and prompt. They refuse a 7-day stop line above 0.85 or an increase above 0.15.

The check and the scorer refuse to run below 25 GiB of free disk space. Before each Protocol B session and before its scoring, the harness waits until 25 GiB are free. It checks every 5 minutes for up to 6 hours. The receipt records each wait.
When 25 GiB are not free after 6 hours, the package stops before the session. Before scoring, the scorer then fails and the outcome is unknown.
The harness records the SHA-256 of evo, evocc and the Kimi CLI at the start. A change before a session or after the last session stops the package.
A live Protocol B run needs --precondition: a passed precondition record with the same binary SHA-256 values.
A stopped Protocol B run reads the quota at the end, unless a quota read stopped it.
An escape stops the package, as in experiments 4 and 5.
An unknown outcome is a final attempt whose status is not completed, timeout or step_limit, a scoring error or an escape. A planned cell without an attempt is unattempted.
The protocol does not say whether the measured run keeps the initial 7-day ratio of the pilot. The owner decides at registration.

amendments.change: T03s (2026-10-16) changed the completion scope of a clean check in full-1 and concise-1 to name the unchecked pointer relations. F is the current full-1, which differs from the experiment 4 and 5 C3 feedback only in that scope sentence. The precondition and the go criteria allow exactly this difference.
amendments.old_scope: No undefined behavior was found on the executed path. This does not check that the results are correct.
amendments.new_scope: No finding from the implemented checks on the executed path. Pointer subtraction and ordering obligations are not checked. This does not check that the results are correct.
